Apple TV: CONNECT's Apple TV app is Connect.Ios.Apple's second target, as CLIENT's is Client.Ios.Apple's (0a5179e2c). Connect.Ios.Apple and Connect.Ios.Extension target VhAppleTargetFrameworks - iOS, and tvOS in a build with -p:VhAppleTv=true - with CLIENT's per-platform lines: the TV's own manifest (Info.tvOS.plist), tvOS 17, tvOS's own libsqlite3 for the split filters, and the guard for a tvOS build without the flag; #if TVOS leaves out the in-app review and the transport of an iPad app on a Mac. VpnHood.AppLib.Stores.AppStore targets tvOS too: Sign in with Apple needs no change there, and StoreKit has no subscription-management sheet on tvOS, so AppStoreBillingProvider.IsSubscriptionManagementSupported is false there and the account page says to manage the subscription from another device, as on an Android TV without a browser; OpenSubscriptionManagement is marked unsupported on tvOS. Its tvOS build needs VpnHood.AppLib.Stores.AppStore.Native 9.0.11, the package's first with tvOS, whose reference follows its publish; iOS keeps 9.0.10 until then. Docs: CONNECT's READMEs (the Apple TV recipe; their docs links and the extension's code location fixed), build-deploy-and-provisioning.md, the root props' comment. Checked on the Mac with the package's tvOS build packed locally: CONNECT's iOS target builds as before; its tvOS one is an Apple TV app with a tvOS extension and the four tvOS StoreKit functions, with no platform warning; both start on a simulator, the terms page drawn, the API answering, the log without an error; the publish reads the bundle id; a tvOS build without the flag stops with the guard's message; a Release device build links, its entitlements aside, which wait for tvOS provisioning profiles.
